description: Agreement between the Swift app's language decision (NLLanguageRecognizer under the gates of language.json) and the Rust core's (whatlang, restricted to the languages NLLanguageRecognizer can answer, under the same letter gate; a Latin- or Cyrillic-script answer admitted only when the text's letters fit its alphabet and its function words point to it alone, HK-425, any other with a confidence above 0.59 on whatlang's scale, HK-421; CJK the core decides by its script alone, HK-423), on natural sentences of the kind replies hold (spec #100 slice 2.5, ticket #160; ADR 0011: the speech text rules are shared, the engines and voices are per OS). expected.swift is the decision the Swift app made (a language code, or null for undecided, read as English). A Rust decision that differs is either resolved toward the Swift one or recorded as an accepted difference: expected gains "core" with the core's decision, the reason says why the difference is accepted, and the ledger names it. Three kinds are accepted: the core undecided, so the reply reads in English (HK-421, HK-422, HK-423, HK-425); CJK text the core decides by its script where the recognizer named another CJK language, so Han-only Japanese reads as Chinese (HK-420), a quoted kana word decides Japanese and hangul Korean (HK-423); and the core naming the language a sentence is written in, the one its case is named after, where the recognizer named another or was undecided (Russian the recognizer read as Kazakh, HK-425). Outside CJK the core never names a language other than the sentence's own. The corpus covers every Latin- and Cyrillic-script language the core can name (en, de, fr, es, it, pt, nl, cs, sk, pl, hr, sv, da, nb, fi, hu, ro, tr, id, vi, ca, ru, uk, bg, with terse English code-review prose among the en sentences), simplified and traditional Chinese, ja, ko, mixed CJK and Latin, full-width forms, texts mixing CJK scripts, short strings, Han-only text, text that is no language, code-heavy prose, and languages the core cannot name (unlisted: the core answers only the languages both whatlang and NLLanguageRecognizer know, HK-422).
